---
title: "Standardised-evidence flags in a league"
subtitle: "3.4 · a simulated league after the postrank theory book, ch. 17"
description: "Pairwise directions and posterior risk of a thirty-unit flag report."
---

The standardised-evidence rule assigns three flags to a league of thirty units. Its reference is the mean of the
thirty estimates, treated as fixed in the calculation. This treatment is a modelling assumption because the reference
is itself estimated. The estimate display and relation matrix identify the directions stated between flag groups,
including reversals of the estimate order. Posterior evaluation then gives the expected errors and risk of that
fixed report. Changing the posterior or withholding cost changes the evaluation without changing the inputs used to
assign the flags.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/temml/temml.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/flags-in-the-league.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["flags-in-the-league"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **League, cutoff 1.96.** The flag groups contain 6, 22 and 2 units. They state 188 of 435 pairs. Under the
  teaching posterior, E/N is .130 and risk is .1696. The grey row bands identify units placed below another unit
  whose estimate is smaller; the outlined matrix cells locate the same reversals.
- **Same flags, flat prior.** The report still states 188 pairs. Error and risk are reevaluated under independent normal posteriors centred on the estimates, with SDs equal to their SEs. Changing the posterior
  changes the evaluation without changing the rule's inputs.
- **League, cutoff 2.576.** The stricter cutoff changes membership of the outer flag groups. The matrix changes in whole blocks:
  all pairs between different flag groups are stated, and all pairs within a group are withheld. A withheld cell
  does not assert equality.
- **Same report, τ .10.** The same 188 pairs are stated. The all-withheld comparison has risk τ = .10. The cheaper baseline depends on the withholding cost even when the report does not change.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
At the first setting, 20 stated directions run against the estimates. The largest stated error is .649, so an
average below the withholding cost does not mean that every individual direction is reliable. These are evaluations
of a fixed report under independent normal posteriors; the flag rule does not optimize this loss and uses neither
τ nor the posterior. The full matrix follows decreasing estimates on both axes. Arrow-key selection and tables provide the cell values and the complete list of reversals.
:::

Standalone: [flags-in-the-league](../../embed/flags-in-the-league.html), for example `?crit=1.96&prior=teaching&tau=.10`.

Related applications: [Grades based on standardised evidence](evidence-flags.qmd), [Posterior summaries in a grade report](../grades/report-card.qmd).
